title: Notifications, channels, and the permission Android 13 introduced

videos.script: A notification is a request. Your code builds one and hands it over, and the system decides whether anybody sees it. {{gates}} Three gates stand in the way. The permission, on Android 13 and later. The student's switch for the whole app. And the channel, whose importance the student controls. The first two fail in silence. {{channel}} So you start with a channel. A name and a sentence the student will read in settings, and an importance you choose once. {{build}} Then the notification itself. A silhouette icon, a title, a line of text, and a tap. {{permission}} Then four phones, one function. Granted, not granted, switched off, and an Android 12 that never heard of the permission. {{tap}} Then the tap, which the system fires for you hours later. One flag it insists on, and one number that keeps two courses apart. {{phone}} And last, what only a phone shows: the dialog, the shade, and the settings screen where your channel's name finally gets read.
